paper: QuantAgents: Towards Multi-agent Financial System via Simulated Trading
claim_boundary: A researcher-authored monthly U.S.-stock implementation of QuantAgents' four roles, three memories, similar-case retrieval, strategy simulation meeting, adaptive simulated/real reward blend, and triggered risk meeting; not a native GPT-4o meeting or learned policy replication.

primary_source_anchors.mechanism: Manager Otto integrates Emily's market reports, Bob's simulated strategy tests, and Dave's risk analysis through weekly market-analysis and strategy-development meetings plus triggered risk alerts.
Market-information, strategy, and report memories retrieve the ten most similar cases to augment a reflection-driven action policy.
Bob simulates a diverse pool of index/parameter strategy permutations on historical information, selects strong candidates, and stores their analysis for later decisions.
A risk score combining beta, inverse liquidity, concentration, and volatility triggers a risk meeting above 0.75 and tilts the policy toward risk reward.
Otto combines new simulated-strategy reward and deployed real-trading reward with adaptive weights based on their recent relative performance.

agents_and_meetings.Otto: Blend the currently deployed and newly simulated strategy sets, integrate Emily's market report, and apply Dave's risk modification.
agents_and_meetings.Bob: Score the strategy pool on ten retrieved similar historical states and propose the three highest simulated-utility strategies.
agents_and_meetings.Dave: Compute equal-weight beta, inverse-liquidity, concentration, and volatility risk and provide a defensive policy when risk exceeds 0.75.
agents_and_meetings.Emily: Summarize sentiment surprises and current price trend into a market-report score.

memory_and_policy.retrieval_distance: Euclidean distance after standardizing every state dimension on the 120-month past-only memory window
memory_and_policy.simulated_utility: mean retrieved-case strategy RankIC minus one half of retrieved-case RankIC standard deviation
memory_and_policy.simulated_reward_weight: sigmoid of trailing simulated-reward sum divided by the sum of absolute simulated and real reward magnitudes
memory_and_policy.deployed_strategy_update: after each decision, the newly simulated three-member set becomes the deployed set for the next month
memory_and_policy.common_portfolio_adapter: frozen value-weighted long-short deciles with all six cost and missing-return paths

preserved_elements: four named manager, strategy, risk, and market-analysis roles
market-analysis and strategy-development meetings every decision period
a risk meeting triggered above the paper's 0.75 score threshold
market-information, strategy, and report memory concepts
retrieval of exactly ten similar historical cases
a diverse strategy pool evaluated in simulated trading
selection of strong simulated strategies before deployment
adaptive blending of simulated and real trading rewards
approximated_elements: five numeric market-state dimensions replace price, news, and report embeddings
JKP factor sleeves replace unreported index/parameter permutations
similar-month RankIC replaces Bob's full simulated portfolio backtests
deterministic market and risk scores replace Emily and Dave LLM/tool reports
explicit strategy-score blending replaces Otto's missing prompt/parser policy
the common decile portfolio replaces unspecified order, fill, and action rules
invented_elements: the ten exact strategy-pool members and signed formulas
the 120-month memory window and standardized Euclidean retrieval
the 12-month adaptive reward window and stable sigmoid denominator
